scope: Single pilot episode only. No other videos inspected.

episode.title: Debate With Arnab LIVE: Nationalists Unite Against Anarchy, No Free Pass For CJP
episode.reference_note: Manually supplied by researcher. Used for evaluation only, never as a rule.

environment.note: Heavy ASR/diarization/topic deps live in the v2 venv and are not re-run during this audit.

confirmed_defects.title: final.json participants array is empty
confirmed_defects.evidence: final.json participants == []; identity/linked.json has num_participants 0 and participants []; no roster/roster.json and no identity/roles.json exist for this episode
confirmed_defects.root_cause: v2/identity/link.py only emits participant rows for entries that already exist in the roster input. With an absent roster.json the roster list is empty, so linked.json is empty. v2/cli/finalize.py copies that empty list verbatim. PENDING_TASKS.md confirms roster extraction/linking is unfinished.
confirmed_defects.impact: No identity/role records reach final.json; downstream participation-by-name and host identity impossible from participants.

confirmed_defects.title: Topic window model probabilities are computed then discarded
confirmed_defects.evidence: topic_modeling.py build_report() attaches 'probability' to each internal assignment (line ~431) but contiguous_runs() keeps only start/end/value/unit_count/speakers. The probability never appears in the output JSON.
confirmed_defects.impact: Window-level confidence is unavailable even though calculate_probabilities=True was used.

confirmed_defects.title: No window-level topic assignment output exists
confirmed_defects.evidence: topic_modeling.json episodes[0] stores only subtopic_timeline / broad_timeline runs. The 138 raw windows (timestamps, text, base_topic_id, probability, speaker ids) are not persisted.
confirmed_defects.impact: Cannot validate assignments, reproduce drift analysis, or inspect the 3256-3310 boundary without recomputing.

confirmed_defects.title: Three segments carry a null speaker
confirmed_defects.evidence: count of segments with empty/None speaker == 3 (of 1605)
confirmed_defects.impact: Minor; topic build_units tolerates it (speakers list empty for those), but participation per segment can miss them.

confirmed_defects.title: Speaker set differs between turns and segments
confirmed_defects.evidence: unique speakers in speaker_turns == 61; unique speakers in segments == 56
confirmed_defects.impact: 5 diarized speakers never own a timed segment; discourse participation counts (from turns, 61 speakers) and topic window speaker lists (from segments, 56 speakers) are not directly comparable.

likely_issues_requiring_validation.title: Generic stopwords in candidate topic labels
likely_issues_requiring_validation.evidence: broad_000 label 'political · cjp · know'; subtopic_001 'dont · german · know'; evidence terms include 'know', 'dont', 'just', 'want'.
likely_issues_requiring_validation.note: TF-IDF/CountVectorizer stop_words='english' is applied in fit_model and top_terms, yet 'know'/'dont' survive. Needs checking whether debate-specific stopwords (discourse fillers) are informative here before removal. Do not assume they are uninformative without reading examples.

likely_issues_requiring_validation.title: Representative examples may be truncated / not representative
likely_issues_requiring_validation.evidence: subtopic representative_example = members[0][:240]; the first document of a cluster is used, not the most central. Subtopic_001 example is about 'Sandesh Kali / Maoist agenda' while its label is 'dont · german · know'.
likely_issues_requiring_validation.note: Representative example and label can disagree; needs cluster-central example selection.

likely_issues_requiring_validation.title: Broad topics are 1:1 with subtopics here
likely_issues_requiring_validation.evidence: 5 broad topics, 5 subtopics, each broad_topic lists exactly one subtopic_id; group_broad_topics returns identity when len(base_ids) <= n_broad (5 <= 8).
likely_issues_requiring_validation.note: The hierarchy is flat for this episode. A hierarchy should not be forced; but the current broad/subtopic split adds no grouping. Report as limitation, not fix blindly.

likely_issues_requiring_validation.title: Ad/intro content is inside the first topic run
likely_issues_requiring_validation.evidence: segments[0..~80] are advertisements ('Your Shahi Paneer Masala', 'Roonta TMT bar'); first broad_timeline run spans 0.051-618.057s labeled broad_003 'republic · chaat · orn'.
likely_issues_requiring_validation.note: trim_config is null; no trim applied. Ad content consumes ~37 windows? (11 windows in first run) and pollutes topic labels.

likely_issues_requiring_validation.title: Topic windows and overlap events are on different time bases
likely_issues_requiring_validation.evidence: windows are 45s-granularity concatenations; overlaps are 1-5s. Around 3256-3310 the window boundary 3302.869/3302.889 coincides with two overlaps 3302.165-3303.869 and 3304.088-3309.134.
likely_issues_requiring_validation.note: Any interruption->topic-drift association must account for window coarseness; proximity is not causation.

likely_issues_requiring_validation.title: Nested overlap candidates present
likely_issues_requiring_validation.evidence: 6 overlap candidates are strictly nested inside another candidate.
likely_issues_requiring_validation.note: discourse_summary.union_duration already unions intervals, so unique elapsed overlap is protected; confirm no double counting in any new drift module.

likely_issues_requiring_validation.title: interruptions (313) are a strict OSD subset of overlap_candidates (403)
likely_issues_requiring_validation.evidence: osd/analysis.json events == interruptions (313); candidates.json candidates == 403 from three-case reconciliation; final.json interruptions take the OSD-only list, not the reconciled list.
likely_issues_requiring_validation.note: The 90 osd_only/diarization candidates that are not OSD interruptions are never eligible as interruptions. Confirm this is intended; document provenance.

likely_issues_requiring_validation.title: final.json differs from final.json.bak only in speaker_turns granularity
likely_issues_requiring_validation.evidence: diff shows .bak has extra short turns near ~6940s; current final.json is the larger/newer file (2.88MB vs 368KB).
likely_issues_requiring_validation.note: The .bak is a stale intermediate; do not treat as ground truth. No deletion planned.

existing_limitations_acknowledged: AGREE/OSD_ONLY/DIARIZATION_ONLY describe detector corroboration; they do not describe semantic agreement between speakers.
Diarization labels (SPEAKER_xx) are not stable identities across episodes and are not mapped to people.
Interruptions are OSD-derived operational attempts, not human-validated interruptions.
Topic labels are model candidate vocabulary, not observed facts; hierarchy is unvalidated.
ASR/diarization errors propagate into topic windows.
No human semantic agreement/disagreement annotations exist.
components_to_leave_unchanged: ASR transcription schema and WhisperX word timing

three-case-reconciliation in osd/candidates.json and its confidence weights
final.json top-level schema v1.0 and field names

existing test suite structure under tests/test_v2_*.py

phase_2_host_identification: Add a new pure module (e.g. v2/identity/host.py) computing per-speaker linguistic + conversational + temporal features from segments/turns/interruptions, discover greeting/moderator phrases from the actual transcript, and emit an interpretable ranked host-candidate JSON (host_identification.json).
Separate 'role' from diarization label; never hardcode SPEAKER_24; compare top prediction to the reference only for scoring.
Do not reuse the coarse roles.py score blindly; expose raw evidence and a confidence band that is explicitly a heuristic, not a calibrated probability.
phase_3_topic_review: Write topic_modeling_review.json (label quality diagnostics, stopword analysis grounded in real examples, central representative examples) and topic_windows.json (full 138-window table with text, base/sub/broad ids, probability, quality flags, speakers, overlap/interruption intersection flags, dropped reason).
Keep the existing compact timeline output intact for compatibility.
phase_4_discourse_validation: Write discourse_summary_review.json re-deriving each requested metric with explicit definition, unit, denominator, provenance, limitation; validate ordering, nesting, zero-duration, duplicates.
phase_5_drift: Write interruption_topic_drift.json linking events to windows with 45s (and 90s sensitivity) outcome windows, non-interruption comparisons, event-level evidence, and explicit uncertainty.
phase_6_integration: Add tests under tests/test_v2_*.py, keep schemas versioned, document exact reproduction commands, and produce a pilot markdown report.

open_questions_for_researcher: Should the first ~618s advertisement/intro block be trimmed for topic modeling (trim_config), or preserved?
Should 5 of the 61 diarized speakers that never own a segment be excluded from participation denominators?
Is the OSD-only interruption list authoritative, or should reconciled candidates define interruptions?
Which ground-truth host reference label is authoritative if SPEAKER_24 later maps to a named person?
